note: Hand-written behaviour of every entry in api.json. tools/gen_contract.py renders docs/reference/api.md, docs/reference/known-issues.md, skill/api-contract.md and skill/constraints.md from this file plus constraints.json. {{key}} is a value from constraints.json (limits or derived); never type a limit as a literal. Every entry cites the firmware source that proves it (paths relative to head_esp32/components/game_engine/src unless prefixed).
conventions: **Failure modes.** Each call fails in one of these ways, shown in the *Bad argument* and *Failure* columns: **raise** (throws a Lua error; uncaught it aborts the hook, see [Hooks](#hooks) for what that does), **false** (returns `false`), **nil, reason** (returns `nil` and a string; test the first value), **no-op** (does nothing).

**Families.** Display and input (`Sprite`, `Text`, `Shape`, `Anim`, `Input`) raise on a wrong argument type. Robot peripherals (`Speaker`, `Servo`, `Led`) never raise: a bad argument returns `false`. `Voice.set_keywords` raises on a non-table list. Status calls (`Timer`, `Ranking`, `Engine`, `print`) validate little.

**Integers.** Arguments documented as integers (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `z`, frame index, Shape coordinates, scale, rotation) raise `number has no integer representation` on a fractional number. `2.0` is accepted. Round with `math.floor(x + 0.5)`.
**Integers are {{lua_int_bits}}-bit on the robot** (`LUA_USE_C89`): `math.maxinteger` is 2^31−1 and integer overflow wraps. Floats are doubles.

**Handles.** `Sprite`, `Text`, `Shape` and `Anim` are userdata; call methods with a colon (`spr:set_pos(x, y)`). `:destroy()` is idempotent; after it every method is a no-op (getters return zeros, boolean methods `false`). Text and Shape no-ops log a warning; Sprite and Anim no-ops are silent.

**Keep a reference to every handle.** Handles have `__gc`: a Sprite, Text, Shape or Anim that no Lua variable references is destroyed at the next garbage collection and disappears from the screen. A dropped Text or Shape keeps its pool slot until then. Handles also support `<close>`. Everything is freed when the game ends.

**Paths** are relative to the pack folder. The engine prefixes `/sd/games/<game_id>/`; the whole path must stay under {{sandbox_path_max}} bytes, so a relative path may use at most {{sandbox_rel_path_budget}} bytes minus the length of the game id. An absolute path, a backslash, a control character, or an empty, `.` or `..` segment (`a//b`, trailing `/`) raises `unsafe ... path`.
**Colours.** `Text` and `Shape` take `0xRRGGBB`. `Sprite.solid` takes 16-bit RGB565. Mixing them gives wrong colours, not an error.
**Reading an unknown field** of an engine global or handle gives `nil` (feature detection works); calling it raises. `pika` is an empty global table.
hooks_intro: Define hooks as globals in the entry script; all are optional. Each call runs under the hook watchdog ({{hook_watchdog_ms}} ms); a call that runs longer raises `watchdog: Lua pcall exceeded ...`. The watchdog is checked every {{watchdog_hook_count}} Lua instructions, so one long native call (a big image load) is only caught when it returns. A separate stall detector ends a game whose frame loop makes no progress for {{stall_detect_sec}} s.

hooks.name: game_start
hooks.when: Once, after the entry script's top level ran and after `on_tick`/`on_input` were bound.
hooks.on_error: Load fails (`game.error phase=load`); `game_end` is not called.

hooks.name: on_tick
hooks.bound: **once**, right after the top level runs

hooks.name: on_input
hooks.when: Once per button event per action bound to that button, before `on_tick` of the same frame.
hooks.bound: **once**, right after the top level runs

hooks.name: on_input_lost
hooks.when: Button events were dropped because the input queue ({{input_ring_slots}} events) overflowed.
hooks.args: `count`: events lost since the last report.

hooks.name: on_sound_end
hooks.when: At the start of the frame after a sound finished, was stopped or was preempted.

hooks.name: on_sound_lost
hooks.when: `on_sound_end` events were dropped because the finish queue ({{sound_finish_ring}} events) overflowed.
hooks.args: `count`: events lost since the last report.

hooks.name: on_voice_event
hooks.when: Between frames, for each voice frame (see [Voice](#voice)).
hooks.args: `e`: table, or the raw JSON string when the frame is not valid JSON or exceeds {{voice_event_max_depth}} levels / {{voice_event_max_nodes}} nodes.
hooks.on_error: Logged; the game continues (the session still reports `end=err`).

hooks.name: on_home
hooks.when: Between frames, on a short press of HOME.
hooks.args: none. Return a truthy value to keep the game running (e.g. to open a pause screen).
hooks.on_error: Game ends (clean exit). `nil`, `false` or a missing hook also end it.

hooks.name: game_end
hooks.when: Once during teardown, however a started game ends (not after a failed load). Runs after `game.stop` is logged.

hooks.name: on_pack_cmd
hooks.when: **Internal, not for game code.** Host command channel of built-in packs.

hook_rules: **Define `on_tick` and `on_input` at the top level of the entry script.** They are bound once, before `game_start` runs; assigning them later (`on_tick = play_tick` inside `game_start` or a scene change) is silently ignored. Switch behaviour with a state variable inside one `on_tick`. Other hooks are looked up at every call.

**Frame order.** Each frame: `on_sound_end`/`on_sound_lost` → `on_input`/`on_input_lost` → `on_tick` → queued servo, LED and sound-stop commands are sent → the active `Anim` advances at most one frame → all display changes are published as one screen update. `on_voice_event` and `on_home` run between frames.

**The display lock is held for the whole tick.** Everything from the sound drain to the screen publish runs under the LVGL lock, so an SD read (`set_frame`), a PNG decode or a long Lua loop in a hook also freezes screen refresh for that time.
**HOME held for {{home_force_exit_ms}} ms or longer force-exits** the game whatever `on_home` returns (`end=home`). Only short presses reach `on_home`.
timing: `dt_ms` is always {{dt_ms}} (1000 / {{target_fps}}), not the measured frame time.

The frame period is {{tick_period_ms}} ms: the RTOS tick is {{freertos_tick_ms}} ms, so the {{dt_ms}} ms target rounds down to whole ticks. That caps the loop at about {{tick_hz_max}} frames per second. A game that adds `dt_ms` every frame therefore runs about 10% fast when frames are on time and slow when they are late. **Use `Timer.millis()` for anything time-based.**

params.meaning: `true` when the game was started inside a talk-flow (A2A) session.
ISO 639-1 code of the robot's UI language, e.g. `"en"`.

Start parameters from the server, decoded from JSON: at most {{start_params_max_bytes}} bytes and {{start_params_max_nodes}} nodes. Longer, malformed or non-object parameters give an empty table plus the two fields above.

calls.name: Engine.exit
calls.bad: raise if `reason` is not a string or number
calls.notes: Schedules a normal stop; the current hook runs to its end, so `return` right after the call. `game_end()` runs during teardown. `reason` (default `"lua"`) is logged.

calls.name: Engine.report_result
calls.bad: raise if the argument is not a table
calls.fail: nil, reason: `bad_event` (missing, empty or over {{report_event_max_bytes}} bytes), `encode_failed`, `payload_too_big`, `send_failed`
calls.notes: **Talk-flow (A2A) only** (`params.is_a2a`). Hands the outcome string (e.g. `"win"`) to the conversation, which receives it when the game ends. Does not end the game. Outside talk-flow nothing uses it.

calls.name: Engine.stack_hwm
calls.notes: **Internal, not for game code.** Firmware stack sizing probe.

calls.name: Timer.millis
calls.notes: Monotonic milliseconds since boot, the only real clock. It is a {{lua_int_bits}}-bit integer and turns negative after about 24.8 days of uptime; compare differences (`now - t0`), never absolute values.

calls.name: print
calls.notes: Writes one line `[lua] a<TAB>b...` to the robot's serial log (arguments through `tostring`). The serial console is slow and the time is spent inside your hook: never print every frame.

Input.intro: Buttons are addressed by the action names declared in `manifest.json` (`input.actions`). Without that block the engine defines `confirm` (enter), `left` and `right`. The robot has three game buttons: `button:left`, `button:enter`, `button:right`. HOME is not an action; it calls `on_home()`.

calls.name: Input.is_down
calls.bad: raise if `action` is missing or not a string
calls.notes: `true` while any button bound to the action is held. Poll it for smooth movement.

calls.name: Input.just_pressed
calls.notes: `true` in the frame the button went down. A press and release in the same frame make `just_pressed` and `just_released` both `true`.

calls.name: Input.just_released
calls.notes: `true` in the frame the button went up.

calls.name: Input.hold_ms
calls.notes: Hold time carried by the last `REPEAT`/`RELEASE` event: `0` until the first `REPEAT` ({{button_repeat_delay_ms}} ms after the press, then every {{button_repeat_rate_ms}} ms), kept at the release value after `RELEASE`, at most 65535. Largest value across bound buttons.

calls.name: Input.actions
calls.notes: Array of action names in manifest order.

calls.name: Input.stats
calls.notes: `{events_total, events_delta, dropped_total, seq_gaps}`. `events_delta`: events since the previous call; `dropped_total`: queue overflows; `seq_gaps`: events lost between the button board and the engine.

constants.name: Input.REPEAT
constants.meaning: Button still held; first after {{button_repeat_delay_ms}} ms, then every {{button_repeat_rate_ms}} ms

after: Compare `phase` with the constants, not with numbers.

Sprite.intro:
Images on the {{screen_w}} × {{screen_h}} screen. There is no sprite count limit; free PSRAM is the limit. PSRAM per sprite: `w*h*3` bytes for a PNG that can carry transparency (RGBA, grey+alpha, or any PNG with a `tRNS` chunk; RGB565 plus an 8-bit alpha plane), `w*h*2` for a PNG without alpha (RGB, grey or palette without `tRNS`), a raw `.rgb565` file or a solid. The engine decides from the PNG header, so an RGBA PNG whose alpha is always 255 still costs `w*h*3`: export opaque images as RGB PNG or `.rgb565`. While a PNG decodes, the whole file is also held in PSRAM.

A new sprite is placed at (0, 0) on top of everything created before it, but **stays hidden until its first `:set_pos` or `:set_visible`**. A sprite you never position is never drawn.

calls.name: Sprite.image
calls.bad: raise on a non-string or unsafe path
calls.fail: nil, msg: e.g. `image load failed: assets/a.png (ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND)` or `(ESP_ERR_NO_MEM)`
calls.notes: Decodes a PNG, keeping its alpha. File at most {{png_max_file_mib}} MiB, image at most {{img_max_w}} × {{img_max_h}}.

calls.name: Sprite.new
calls.bad: raise on a non-string or unsafe path, or non-integer `w`/`h`
calls.notes: Loads raw RGB565 pixels (2 bytes per pixel, little-endian, row-major, no header); the file must hold at least `w*h*2` bytes. At most {{img_max_w}} × {{img_max_h}}. Cheapest opaque image and the usual base for frame strips.

calls.name: Sprite.solid
calls.bad: raise when `w` is not 1..{{img_max_w}} or `h` not 1..{{img_max_h}}
calls.notes: Filled rectangle, no file. The colour is **RGB565** (`0xF800` red, `0x07E0` green, `0x001F` blue); only the low 16 bits are used.

calls.name: Sprite:set_pos
calls.notes: Top-left corner in screen pixels; off-screen is allowed. Also makes a new sprite visible.

calls.name: Sprite:get_pos
calls.bad: raise if `spr` is not a sprite

calls.name: Sprite:get_size
calls.notes: Source size; `set_scale` does not change it.

calls.name: Sprite:set_visible
calls.notes: Truthiness of `b`.

calls.name: Sprite:set_opacity
calls.notes: 0..255, rounded and clamped.

calls.name: Sprite:set_z
calls.notes: Moves the object to child index `i` of the screen. Sprites, Text labels, Shape lines and Anim canvases share one list; a larger index draws on top. `i` is clamped to `0..count-1`, so a large value means "top".

calls.name: Sprite:to_front
calls.notes: Same as the highest index.

calls.name: Sprite:to_back
calls.notes: Same as index 0.

calls.name: Sprite:set_flip
calls.notes: Sets the absolute flip state (not a toggle) by rewriting every pixel (O(w·h)), and only when the state differs from the recorded one. Call it on state changes, not every frame. **Do not combine with `set_frame`** ([KI-FLIP-FRAME](@docs/reference/known-issues.md#ki-flip-frame)).

calls.name: Sprite:set_frame
calls.bad: raise on unsafe path or non-integer `i`
calls.fail: `false` when the file is missing or `i` is past the end
calls.notes: Overwrites the pixels with frame `i` (0-based) of a **raw strip file**: frames stored back to back in the sprite's own pixel format, `w*h*2` bytes per frame for `Sprite.new`, `Sprite.solid` and an opaque PNG sprite, `w*h*3` for a PNG sprite with alpha. Never a PNG file: a PNG path is read as raw bytes and shows garbage. Reads the SD card on every call, under the display lock.

calls.name: Sprite:set_scale
calls.fail: `false` when the sprite is too large to transform
calls.notes: `256` = 1×, `512` = 2×, `128` = ½×. Clamped to 1..4096, then to `{{img_max_w}}*256 / max(w, h)` so the scaled sprite fits the screen width. See [Transform limit](#transform-limit).

calls.name: Sprite:set_rotation
calls.fail: `false` when the sprite is too large to transform
calls.notes: Tenths of a degree (`900` = 90°), wraps modulo 3600.

calls.name: Sprite:set_pivot
calls.notes: Origin of scale and rotation in sprite-local pixels; default is the centre. Not size-checked, but has no effect on a sprite that cannot be transformed.

calls.name: Sprite:hit_test
calls.notes: Point inside `[x, x+w) × [y, y+h)`. Ignores visibility, scale and rotation.

calls.name: Sprite:intersects
calls.bad: raise if `other` is not a sprite
calls.notes: Axis-aligned rectangles overlap. Same rules as `:hit_test`.

calls.name: Sprite:destroy
calls.notes: Frees the pixels now. Idempotent.

after: `:set_scale` and `:set_rotation` work only when **both** the sprite's width and height are at most {{transform_max_px}} px (`transform_max_px`). Larger sprites return `false`, nothing changes, and the refusal is logged once per sprite: `set_scale refused: sprite WxH exceeds {{transform_max_px}} px transform limit`. Transforms are applied at draw time and cost CPU every frame the sprite is drawn: use them for short effects.

Text.intro: Retained text labels. At most {{text_slots}} exist at a time (`text_slots`). Text does not wrap and there is no width query: break lines in your data with `\n` and check the longest string in the simulator.

calls.name: Text.new
calls.fail: nil, `"pool_full"` ({{text_slots}} labels live, or out of memory) or `"text_create_failed"`
calls.notes: Shown immediately, top-left at (x, y), white, default font.

calls.name: Text:set
calls.notes: Changes the text. A string under 64 bytes that equals the current one is skipped by the engine; the cost left is building the string in Lua.

calls.name: Text:move
calls.notes: Absolute top-left position.

calls.name: Text:align
calls.notes: Aligns to the screen. `where`: `center`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `top_left`, `top_right`, `bottom_left`, `bottom_right`; `dx`, `dy` offset in px (default 0).

calls.name: Text:set_font
calls.fail: nil, msg: unsafe path, bad file, stale label, or font cache full
calls.notes: TrueType font from the pack, file at most {{font_max_file_kib}} KiB. `size` in px, default {{font_px_default}}, clamped to {{font_px_min}}..{{font_px_max}}. See [Fonts](#fonts).

calls.name: Text:set_color
calls.notes: `0xRRGGBB`.

calls.name: Text:show
calls.notes: Show or hide.

calls.name: Text:destroy
calls.notes: Frees the slot for a new `Text.new`. Idempotent.

after: A face is a (path, size) pair. The engine caches at most {{font_slots}} faces; labels using the same pair share one. A face used by a live label cannot be evicted, so a fifth distinct pair fails until a label using another face is destroyed or switched. Ship every font the pack uses; the default font does not cover every script.
Text has no `set_z`. Its stacking is its creation order, changed only when other objects call `:set_z`, `:to_front` or `:to_back`. Create labels last to keep them on top.

Shape.intro: Straight line segments. Each line is rasterised once into an anti-aliased image over its bounding box; changing geometry or style re-rasterises it. Good for a few long strokes (paths on a map, dividers), not for many short ones.

calls.name: Shape.line
calls.bad: raise on non-integer or out-of-range coordinate, or bad `style`
calls.notes: Screen coordinates, `x` in −{{img_max_w}}..{{x2_max}}, `y` in −{{img_max_h}}..{{y2_max}}. Shown immediately.

calls.name: Shape:set_points
calls.notes: Moves the endpoints; the same points again cost nothing. On failure the line keeps its old picture.

calls.name: Shape:set_style
calls.bad: raise on a non-table or bad field
calls.notes: Replaces the **whole** style: omitted fields return to their defaults.

calls.name: Shape:set_opacity
calls.notes: 0..255, clamped.

calls.name: Shape:set_z
calls.notes: Same child index as `spr:set_z`.

calls.name: Shape:set_visible
calls.notes: Show or hide.

calls.name: Shape:destroy
calls.notes: Frees the slot and its raster budget. Idempotent.

after:
| Reason | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `pool_full` | {{line_slots}} lines already exist (`line_slots`) |
| `bbox_too_large` | Bounding box plus padding (4 px + half the width on each side) exceeds {{img_max_w}} × {{img_max_h}} |
| `no_mem` | All lines together would exceed the {{line_pool_kib}} KiB raster budget (`bbox_w * bbox_h * 3` bytes per line), or PSRAM is exhausted |
| `shape_create_failed` | Screen not available |

| Field | Type | Default | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | integer | `2` | Clamped to 1..{{line_width_max}} |
| `color` | integer | `0xFFFFFF` | `0xRRGGBB` |
| `dash` | `{on, off}` | solid | Exactly two integers, each 0..{{img_max_w}}; a `0` draws solid. Anything else raises. |
| `cap` | string | `"butt"` | `"butt"` or `"round"`; anything else raises. |

Anim.intro: Plays a GIF or MJPEG file (`.gif`, `.mjpeg`, `.mjpg`, case-insensitive). Several Anims can be loaded; only one plays at a time. Each loaded Anim holds its whole file plus a `w*h*2` canvas in PSRAM until destroyed. The canvas is opaque RGB565 with no alpha and starts black (`render/lvgl_renderer.c` `renderer_sprite_create_blank`): transparent GIF pixels show black, not what is behind the Anim.

calls.name: Anim.new
calls.bad: raise on unknown extension or unsafe path
calls.notes: Loads the file (at most {{anim_max_file_mib}} MiB) and creates the canvas; frame size at most {{img_max_w}} × {{img_max_h}}. Stops nothing. The canvas is hidden at (0, 0) until `:play`, `:set_pos` or `:set_visible`.

calls.name: Anim:play
calls.bad: raise if `a` is not an anim
calls.notes: `a:play()` plays once; `a:play(true)` or `a:play{loop = true}` loops. Stops (and rewinds) any other playing Anim, shows the canvas and draws a frame at once. Rewinds to the first frame only if this Anim had ended (a finished one-shot or after `:stop`); on a paused or playing Anim it continues from the current frame.

calls.name: Anim:pause
calls.notes: Freezes on the current frame.

calls.name: Anim:resume
calls.notes: Continues after `:pause`; stops any other playing Anim.

calls.name: Anim:stop
calls.notes: Stops and rewinds; the last frame stays on screen until hidden.

calls.name: Anim:is_playing
calls.notes: `false` once a one-shot reaches its last frame: poll it to detect the end.

calls.name: Anim:set_pos
calls.notes: Top-left corner.

calls.name: Anim:set_visible
calls.notes: Show or hide.

calls.name: Anim:destroy
calls.notes: Frees the file buffer and canvas. Idempotent.

after: The engine advances the playing Anim by at most one frame per engine frame, so its rate is capped by the frame rate. Frame delays below {{anim_min_frame_ms}} ms are raised to {{anim_min_frame_ms}} ms. A decode error mid-playback stops it (counted as `animerr` in `game.warn`).

Speaker.intro: Sounds are aliases declared in `manifest.json` (`audio.sounds`). There is **one channel**: a new `Speaker.play` preempts the current sound, which then receives `on_sound_end(alias, Speaker.REASON_PREEMPTED)`. There is no text-to-speech; every spoken line is a recorded file.

calls.name: Speaker.play
calls.fail: `false`: unknown alias, remote alias without a URL yet, within {{sound_cooldown_ms}} ms of the previous play (`cooldown_reject`), or audio request refused
calls.notes: The automatic restart of a looping sound counts as a play for the cooldown.

calls.name: Speaker.stop
calls.fail: `false` if `alias` is not the sound currently playing
calls.notes: `on_sound_end(alias, Speaker.REASON_STOPPED)` arrives at the start of the **next** frame, also when called from inside `on_sound_end`.

calls.name: Speaker.stop_all
calls.notes: Silences everything. The tracked current sound receives `REASON_STOPPED` next frame.

calls.name: Speaker.is_playing
calls.notes: `true` while `alias` is the current game sound, by engine bookkeeping (a prediction, not a hardware signal).

calls.name: Speaker.is_busy
calls.notes: `true` while the speaker plays anything, including non-game audio.

calls.name: Speaker.set_url
calls.fail: `false` for a `path` alias, an undeclared alias or a bad URL
calls.notes: Sets or overrides the URL of an alias declared with `"remote": true` or `"url"`. `url` must start with `http://` or `https://` (https is rewritten to http), contain only printable non-space ASCII and be at most {{sound_url_chars}} bytes.

calls.name: Speaker.set_volume
calls.notes: 0..100, rounded and clamped. The user's volume is restored when the game ends.

calls.name: Speaker.get_volume
calls.notes: The volume set by the game this session, else the user's saved volume.

calls.name: Speaker.stats
calls.notes: `{played_total, finish_dropped, error_count, cooldown_reject, no_hookup, speaker_abandoned_current, speaker_abandoned_peak}`. `finish_dropped`: `on_sound_end` events lost; `no_hookup`: plays that will never report `on_sound_end` because too many plays were in flight.

after: A sound declared `"loop": true` restarts on completion and never fires `REASON_COMPLETED`; stop it with `Speaker.stop`.

```lua
function on_sound_end(alias, reason)
  if alias == "intro" and reason == Speaker.REASON_COMPLETED then
    start_round()
  end
end
```

Servo.intro: Moves the robot's joints. Aliases come from `servos` and `poses` in `manifest.json`. Commands are queued and sent after `on_tick`; two moves of the same servo in one frame are merged. Results are local predictions, not hardware acknowledgements.

calls.name: Servo.pose
calls.fail: `false` for an unknown alias or a full queue
calls.notes: Plays the gesture mapped to a pose alias and marks all four servos busy for about 1.5 s.

calls.name: Servo.move
calls.notes: Moves one servo. `angle` in degrees, `duration_ms` 0..65535 (both saturated). `easing`: `"linear"` (default), `"in_out"`, `"bounce"`; anything else returns `false`.

calls.name: Servo.stop
calls.notes: Stops one servo, or all four without an argument (works even without a `servos` block; `true` only if every stop was queued).

calls.name: Servo.is_busy
calls.notes: Predicted from the requested duration, not a hardware signal: fine for "do not queue while moving", not for exact choreography.

calls.name: Servo.list
calls.notes: `{servos = {alias = "head"|"base"|"left"|"right"}, poses = {alias = gesture}}`.

calls.name: Servo.stats
calls.notes: `{pushed_total, coalesced_total, dropped_total, sent_total, send_fail_total, back_reject_throttle, back_reject_validation, back_reject_priority, back_reject_queue_full, last_reject_ms, drain_max_us}`; `back_reject_*` count commands the robot refused, by cause.

Led.intro: The robot's RGB light. Commands are queued and sent after `on_tick`; the light returns to its previous state when the game ends. Every call returns `false` on bad arguments and never raises.

calls.name: Led.set
calls.notes: Each channel 0..255, rounded and clamped.

calls.name: Led.preset
calls.notes: One of `user_talk`, `conv_processing`, `robot_talking`, `warm_white`, `light_blue`, `dark_blue`.

calls.name: Led.blink
calls.notes: Rejected, not clamped: at most 3 flashes per second (photosensitivity limit).

calls.name: Led.pulse
calls.notes: Lights for `duration_ms`, then turns off.

calls.name: Led.get_brightness
calls.notes: Last brightness queued successfully (100 until set); not read back from the hardware.

calls.name: Led.is_available
calls.notes: `true` while the game is running; `false` during the top level and `game_start`.

calls.name: Led.stats
calls.notes: `{pushed_total, coalesced_total, dropped_total, sent_total, send_fail_total, brightness_pct}`.

Voice.intro:
English keyword spotting: the game sends a short list of command words, the robot listens and reports which one it heard. Not free speech recognition. The pack must list `"voice"` in `peripherals`; otherwise no voice session exists. When it is listed, voice is a hard requirement: if the robot cannot keep the voice connection, it ends the game.

**Start voice from `on_tick`, never from the top level or `game_start`.** The robot sets up the voice session only after `game_start` has returned and drops every voice command queued before that, so keywords sent from `game_start` are lost and nothing is ever heard. Send them in the first `on_tick` (or later, on a scene change).

calls.name: Voice.set_keywords
calls.bad: raise if `list` is not a table or `sensitivity` is not a number
calls.fail: nil, reason: `keywords_not_array` (empty table, holes or non-integer keys), `too_many_keywords` (over {{voice_keywords_max}}), `too_deep`, `too_many_keys`, `encode_failed` (a function, userdata or thread inside), `payload_too_big` (the whole encoded body over {{voice_body_max_bytes}} bytes), `send_failed`
calls.notes: Sends the vocabulary **and starts listening**; opening a session (not in talk-flow) stops the sound that is playing, to keep the speaker out of the microphone. `list`: array of up to {{voice_keywords_max}} strings; element types are not checked, so pass strings only. `sensitivity` is truncated to an integer and passed to the voice server unchecked. `true` only means the request was queued; a refusal arrives as an `error` event. While a session is connecting or listening, a second call is refused with `error`/`busy` and the old list stays: to change words call `Voice.stop()`, then `set_keywords` (the robot reconnects, which takes up to a few seconds).

calls.name: Voice.start
calls.notes: Not needed: `set_keywords` already starts listening. While listening it does nothing; when idle it produces an `error`/`no_keywords` event. It cannot resume after `Voice.stop()`; call `set_keywords` again. In talk-flow it always does nothing.

calls.name: Voice.stop
calls.notes: Stops listening and closes the session. Idempotent.

calls.name: Voice.is_available
calls.notes: `true` while the game is running (`false` during the top level and `game_start`). It does not probe the voice service; failures arrive as events.

after: Each voice frame arrives as `on_voice_event(e)`, decoded from JSON into a table (arrays 1-based, `null` becomes absent). A frame that is not valid JSON or exceeds {{voice_event_max_depth}} levels or {{voice_event_max_nodes}} nodes arrives as the raw string, so check `type(e)`.

| Frame | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `e.type == "VOICE_COMMAND"`, `e.data.keyword` | A keyword from the list was heard. *Shape set by the voice server, not yet confirmed against it ([Q-VOICE-SHAPE](@skill/open-questions.md#q-voice-shape)).* |
| `e.type == "VOICE_COMMAND"`, `e.data.status == "unavailable"` | Keyword spotting is down on the server: hide voice hints, keep playing on buttons. |
| `e.type == "error"`, `e.code`, `e.message` | Generated by the robot. `e.code` is one of the codes below. |

| `e.code` | Cause | Game |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `busy` | `set_keywords` while a session is active, or the microphone is in use | continues; the old list stays |
| `no_keywords` | `Voice.start()` with no list sent | continues |
| `no_session_key` | the robot's session key is renewing | continues; retry later with `set_keywords` |
| `invalid_payload` | keyword body too large for the robot | continues |
| `send_failed` | the keyword list could not be sent | continues |
| `connect_failed`, `connect_timeout`, `ws_disconnected`, `ws_error` | the voice connection failed | **ends** |

```lua
local voice_sent = false

function on_tick(dt_ms)
  if not voice_sent then            -- never in game_start: it would be dropped
    voice_sent = true
    Voice.set_keywords({ "jump", "fire", "stop" })
  end
end

function on_voice_event(e)
  if type(e) ~= "table" then return end
  if e.type == "VOICE_COMMAND" and type(e.data) == "table" then
    if e.data.keyword then handle_command(e.data.keyword)
    elseif e.data.status == "unavailable" then hide_voice_hints() end
  elseif e.type == "error" and e.code ~= "busy" then
    hide_voice_hints()
  end
end
```

Ranking.intro: Leaderboard of the robot game platform. Lua cannot write files; this is the only way to keep a score beyond the session.

calls.name: Ranking.report
calls.bad: `false` when the argument is not a table or `score` is not a number
calls.notes: Submits a score; the engine adds the session duration itself. Callable several times per session (e.g. per level). `true` only means the report left the head board: the robot drops it when the game was not started from the menu, and in talk-flow it goes to the conversation instead of the leaderboard, so no result follows.

calls.name: Ranking.get_result
calls.notes: The leaderboard fetched after the last successful report, or `nil` if none arrived yet. **Consume-once**: the next call returns `nil` until a new result arrives. Poll it from `on_tick`.

after: Result table: `{top = {{rank, profile_id, display_name, score, played_at}, ...}, my_rank = {...} or nil, my_best_score = number or nil}`. A result larger than 256 JSON nodes is dropped (`nil`).

sandbox: Available: the Lua 5.5 base library without `load`, `loadfile` and `dofile`; `string`, `table`, `math`, `utf8`. Not available: `io`, `os`, `debug`, `package`, `coroutine`. Only text chunks load; precompiled bytecode is refused.
`require("libs/<name>")` loads `libs/<name>.lua` from the pack once per session (later calls return the cached value). Any other module name raises.

The Lua heap is {{lua_heap_kb}} KiB, garbage included; an allocation past it raises a memory error (in `on_tick` the game ends with `err=OOM`). Image, animation, font and line pixels live in PSRAM outside this heap.

Nested C calls are limited to {{lua_maxccalls}} levels (desktop Lua: 200). `pcall`, metamethods, `table.sort`/`string.gsub` callbacks and `require` each add a level; deeper nesting raises `C stack overflow`. The parser uses the same counter: a single expression with more than about 20 chained `..` or deeply nested table constructors fails to load on the robot.

not_exist.name: Engine.version()
not_exist.instead: nothing; do not print a version from Lua

not_exist.name: State.save(), State.load(), any save API
not_exist.instead: none: nothing persists between sessions; keep scores with `Ranking.report`

not_exist.instead: none: every spoken line is a recorded file

not_exist.instead: `spr:set_opacity(0..255)`; bake tint, blend and gradients into the image

not_exist.instead: `Text.new`, or bake the text into the image

not_exist.instead: break lines in the data; stack with other objects' `:set_z`

not_exist.instead: not loaded; use a state variable and `on_tick`

limits.label: Hook watchdog
limits.past: the hook raises; see each hook's error rule

limits.label: Sprites
limits.value: no count cap; PSRAM `w*h*3` (PNG with alpha) or `w*h*2` (others)

limits.label: Anim
limits.value: 1 playing; file ≤ {{anim_max_file_mib}} MiB; frame delay ≥ {{anim_min_frame_ms}} ms

limits.label: Button repeat
limits.value: first after {{button_repeat_delay_ms}} ms, then every {{button_repeat_rate_ms}} ms

limits.label: Sound aliases
limits.past: **whole pack rejected** (also for a missing sound file)

facts: **No persistence.** Lua cannot write files and there is no save API; scores leave the robot only through `Ranking.report`.
**No TTS.** Every spoken line is a recorded audio file.
**No runtime blend, filter or gradient.** Bake them into the image.
**No text wrap and no width query.** Break lines in the data.
**Draw order is creation order.** `set_z` is a child index shared by Sprites, Text, Shapes and Anim canvases.
**Asynchronous peripherals.** `Servo`, `Led`, `Voice` and `Ranking` return a local result, not a hardware or server acknowledgement. Only `Speaker` reports completion (`on_sound_end`).

**Checksums.** An installed pack carries `s.json` (CRCs of its scripts, JSON and media files), issued when the pack is published through the Pika platform. The robot refuses files that do not match. Never create or edit `s.json`; Pika Studio neither creates nor checks it.
known_issues_intro: Firmware behaviour that is surprising or wrong today. Game code must work around it; each entry says how. IDs are stable: cite them in code comments and bug reports.

known_issues.title: `set_frame` drops the flip but the engine still thinks it is flipped
known_issues.behaviour: `spr:set_frame` loads the frame unflipped but keeps the recorded flip state, and `spr:set_flip` only acts when the requested state differs from the recorded one. After `set_frame`, calling `set_flip` with the same values does nothing, so the frame stays unflipped.
known_issues.workaround: Do not flip sprites that use `set_frame`: ship pre-flipped frames in the strip. If you must: call `set_flip(false, false)` **before** each `set_frame`, then `set_flip` with the wanted state after it.

known_issues.title: `dt_ms` is {{dt_ms}} but frames are {{tick_period_ms}} ms apart
known_issues.behaviour: The frame period rounds to {{tick_period_ms}} ms (RTOS tick {{freertos_tick_ms}} ms) while `on_tick` always receives {{dt_ms}}. Summing `dt_ms` runs about 10% fast on time and drifts whenever frames are late.
known_issues.workaround: Drive every timer and movement from `Timer.millis()` differences.
known_issues.status: confirmed in code; robot logs never show tick_hz above {{tick_hz_max}}

known_issues.title: Near the heap limit a game may be tagged OOM
known_issues.behaviour: The allocator records an OOM error before Lua's emergency garbage collection retries the allocation. A game whose heap, garbage included, touches {{lua_heap_kb}} KiB pays a full-GC hitch and can end with `err=OOM` even though the retry could have succeeded.
known_issues.workaround: Keep peak heap well below the limit: allocate once, reuse tables, avoid building strings every frame. Watch `arena` in `game.running` and `arena_pk` in `game.stop`.
known_issues.status: from code reading, not reproduced on a robot

known_issues.title: `Timer.millis()` turns negative after about 24.8 days
known_issues.behaviour: Integers are {{lua_int_bits}}-bit; uptime in milliseconds overflows after 2^31 ms. A firmware comment claims 49.7 days; that figure is for unsigned 32-bit.
known_issues.workaround: Compare differences (`Timer.millis() - t0`), which stay correct across the wrap.

known_issues.title: The first `game.running` line covers one frame
known_issues.behaviour: The telemetry window starts at the first tick, so the first `game.running` line is printed at `t=0` with a meaningless `tick_hz` (often single digits).
known_issues.workaround: Ignore the first `game.running` line of a session.
known_issues.status: confirmed in code and robot logs

pc_vs_robot_intro: Where the PC tools (`tools/smoke.py`, the browser kit, Pika Studio) behave differently from the robot. Passing on the PC does not prove these points; each row says what to do.

pc_vs_robot.pc: smoke.py (lupa) and Pika Studio use 64-bit integers

pc_vs_robot.do: No deep `pcall`/metamethod/`require` chains; no expression with ~20 chained `..`; smoke.py warns on long `..` chains.

pc_vs_robot.robot: {{tick_period_ms}} ms frames; SD reads and decodes block the frame
pc_vs_robot.pc: a desktop CPU; nothing measures robot cost

pc_vs_robot.robot: keywords sent from `game_start` are dropped; real server
pc_vs_robot.pc: smoke.py flags voice calls in `game_start`; Studio uses its own voice server settings
pc_vs_robot.do: Send keywords from `on_tick`; test voice on a robot.

pc_vs_robot.pc: the browser kit counts every `Sprite.image` at `w*h*3`
pc_vs_robot.do: Trust smoke.py's figure (it reads the PNG header); the kit over-estimates.

pc_vs_robot.robot: `set_frame` works on any sprite whose strip matches its own format
pc_vs_robot.pc: the browser kit supports `set_frame` only on `Sprite.new` `.rgb565` sprites
pc_vs_robot.do: Use `.rgb565` strips; the kit rule is a simplification, not an engine limit.

pc_vs_robot.robot: packs live under `{{games_root}}`, so full paths stay short
pc_vs_robot.pc: Pika Studio builds `<games folder>/<game_id>/<path>` into the engine's {{sound_abs_path_max}}-byte sound path buffer; a long games folder fails the pack at load (`sound '<alias>': bad absolute path`, `game.error code=PACK_MANIFEST`) although it runs on the robot
pc_vs_robot.do: Keep the games folder path at most {{pc_games_root_chars}} characters (e.g. `E:/pika-games`); `tools/smoke.py` warns `PC-ROOT-LEN` for the folder the pack is in.

pc_vs_robot.robot: real hardware; HOME held ≥ {{home_force_exit_ms}} ms force-exits
pc_vs_robot.do: Check them in the release checklist on a robot.

pc_vs_robot.robot: refuses files that do not match `s.json`
pc_vs_robot.do: Publish through the Pika platform; never edit `s.json`.
